note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.” That is the resist: resist the pleasure of sin. It is also in Hebrews, where the saints are striving against sin and resisting it. You are resisting sin.

James said it just before: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” If your eye is single, what are you resisting? All your appetites and all the lust you have. If your eye is single, you are on that path: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

The opposite is the double-minded man: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” You are looking at the Lord and you are looking at Pornhub; you are looking at the Lord and you are in the midst of sin. “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. When your eye is not single, you hate God, because something else has your attention and your draw.

A brother who would not resist shows where it goes. It started with handing his phone to a woman at work while another brother stood a few feet away, no fear at all, and it spiralled into porn, the strip club and fornication. His heart was full of darkness: “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

That is why Peter says “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the fleshly lust comes from what you look at, “the lust of the eyes”. You are at war, brothers, and if you are not resisting you are losing, while Satan is in your head saying you got it under control. The one who resists the pleasure crowns his life.

precepts.text: Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite: which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. His parents did not like his marriage choices of those Hittites. Listen: you have unlearned Israelites that use these verses to say Esau was black because his kids mixed with the Hittites. No. God kept that line the way it is. Even today, no matter how black you are, if you marry a white woman you can tell that child is hybrid: high yellow, sometimes yellow hair, green eyes. Photos shown of Drake as a boy and his family: his hair is like his father, but his complexion is closer to the mother. So you mean back then God could not maintain that same lighter red complexion in Esau's line? These hybrid children look more like Esau.
precepts.point: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. In that pottage was meat: feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage, raw, bloody meat. And you have brothers today lusting after these same people. Many times brothers ask what it means that Esau was profane or a fornicator; the scriptures explain it.
precepts.why:
Hebrews calls Esau a “fornicator, or profane person”, and brothers often ask what that means. The scriptures explain it, beginning with his marriages: “Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.” His parents did not like his choice of those Hittite women.

Some unlearned Israelites use these two verses to say Esau was black, because his children were mixed with the Hittites. No. God kept that line the way it is. Even today, no matter how black you are, if you marry a white woman you can tell the child is a hybrid: high yellow, sometimes yellow hair, green eyes. Look at Drake as a boy with his family: his hair is like his father's, but his complexion is closer to his mother's.

So you mean back then God could not maintain that same look, that lighter red complexion, in Esau's line? No, God don't have that power? Shut up, Negro. Be quiet. These hybrid children look more like Esau. Mixing with the Hittites did not make Esau black; it is part of what made him a fornicator.

precepts.text: Esau, seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father, went unto Ishmael, and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son to be his wife. So now he married Arab kids too; that is what Esau was doing.
precepts.point: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. In that pottage was meat: feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage, raw, bloody meat. And you have brothers today lusting after these same people. Many times brothers ask what it means that Esau was profane or a fornicator; the scriptures explain it.
precepts.why:
After the Hittite wives, Esau went further: “Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father; Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.”

Esau saw that Isaac was pissed off that he married the daughters of Canaan, and instead of turning back to his own kindred, he went to Ishmael. So now he married Arab kids too. That is what Esau was doing: taking wives outside his father's tribe, one after another.

That is the fornication Hebrews 12:16 names. Esau married the Hittites and the Ishmaelites, strange women, and he was profane because for “one morsel of meat” he sold his birthright; it meant a lot, and he did not care about it.

precepts.text: Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe. Whoredom falls under fornication; this is what made Esau a fornicator: he married Hittite women and Ishmaelite women, and Ishmael was the beginning of another race; Genesis is the beginning of races. For we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
precepts.point: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. In that pottage was meat: feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage, raw, bloody meat. And you have brothers today lusting after these same people. Many times brothers ask what it means that Esau was profane or a fornicator; the scriptures explain it.
precepts.why:
Tobit 4:12 shows why Esau is called a fornicator: “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe.” Whoredom falls under fornication. Esau married Hittite women and Ishmaelite women, strange women not of his father's tribe.

Ishmael was the beginning of another race; Genesis is the beginning of races. Tobit goes on: “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

So the fathers married within their own kindred and were blessed in their children; Esau did not. Then there is the profaneness. Hebrews says he sold his birthright “for one morsel of meat”, and that shows what was in the pottage. When Esau came in from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”, he wanted it as it was, raw, red and bloody. “therefore was his name called Edom”, which means red. He said, “Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?” and “thus Esau despised his birthright.” And there are brothers today lusting after these same people and having children with them.

That is why, “when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected”: rejected by God, “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.”

precepts.text: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.
precepts.point: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto. Blessed are the peacemakers, but peace does not always work with some people; some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don't want peace with you.
precepts.why:
Onias’s attributes are the attributes of a man of God. He went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all.” Hebrews tells us to walk the same way: “Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.”

Follow peace with all men, and holiness with it. Without them no man shall see the Lord. You cannot see the Lord walking in Simon’s spirit of malice, slander and murder.

Onias followed peace and holiness even when his friend Simon turned on him, and soon after his own blood brother Jason labored underhand to take the priesthood from him. Put yourself in his sandals. He still sought peace, until he saw it was impossible for the state to stay quiet and Simon to leave his folly unless the king looked into it.

precepts.text: An officer tied it back to the fire: the furnace proveth the potter's vessels, so the trial of man is in his reasoning. When the Lord turns up the heat, he is trying your heart, and your reasoning gets revealed. You lost the job, and now you want to pick up a job on the Sabbath: your reasoning is off; covetousness is revealed. You get checked and you argue and have strife: ego is revealed. As the fire goes up in your life, different spirits rise to the top like metal in the melt. He is dealing with you as a son; are you going to respect him as a father? That is why it says take it cheerfully: you are getting purged as he tries your reasoning, and you get to show forth whether everything you have been hearing is actually being learned and applied.
precepts.point: For what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? As a father you have to correct your son, because if you do not correct him, you do not love him; and as a father you want to see your son do better than you. It is the same in the truth: the heads of the school are fathers over the congregation and treat you as sons, and our leadership are fathers over us; we get chastised just as much as you do, if not more. But that is out of love. And some will turn their back to that and take their ball and go home.
precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” That correction, that chastisement, is the Lord trying your heart, seeing what your heart is made out of. Sirach ties it back to the fire: “The furnace proveth the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.”

The furnace proves the potter’s vessel, but what is the Lord proving? A man’s reasoning. When the Lord turns up the heat on your behind, he is going to try your heart. You have a couple of flat tires, you lost a job, and now you want to pick up a job on the Sabbath. Your reasoning is off, and now it is revealed: covetous. You can’t deal with your lowest state. Or you get checked, maybe it wasn’t exactly your fault, and you don’t take the low; you argue, you have strife. That is ego, and the fire revealed your thoughts.

When the potter melts the metal, each metal has a different temperature to melt and be purged. So as the fire goes up in your life, different spirits are going to come out and rise to the top. He is trying your reasoning. Are you going to deal with it or not? He is dealing with you as a son; are you going to respect him as a father?

That is why you take it cheerfully: you are getting purged as he tries your reasoning, and you get to show forth your understanding, whether everything you have been hearing is actually being learned and applied. And the trial shows other things too. Many like to suffer in silence, and the Lord is showing you your communication is weak. “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another.” When you are going through things, lean on the brothers; call and say I am struggling in this area. Out of pride we suffer in silence, get offended with everybody, and find ourselves out the door.

If he did not love us, he would cut us off, as he cut off Esau, whom he hates. You are supposed to go through it. Three flat tires? You have one more tire than you deserve. A whole kingdom is waiting on us, the world turned right side up, and we have to push through it manfully, together, or not at all.

precepts.text: He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil: so why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think we are moving in the spirit of Christ? In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. If there is an offense, Matthew 18:15: you do not sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit.
precepts.point: For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Hebrews warns of the “root of bitterness springing up”, and John shows what spirit jumps on you when you move that way. “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” That is the history being drawn out from Cain to Esau: the devil sinned from the beginning, and the same spirit runs down through his children.

“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.” The purpose of Christ is to destroy the works of the devil. So why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think that we are moving in the spirit of Christ?

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God.” This is the manifestation of the children of God. If you don't do righteousness, you are not of God. The scripture tells us how to deal uprightly with our brother and sister: if there is an offense, go by Matthew 18:15. You don't sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit through our brothers and sisters.

“neither he that loveth not his brother.” When you don't love your brother, you are not moving in the spirit of Christ and you are not counted a child of God. You are the son and daughter of Cain, of Esau. We have to be mindful of this spirit and purge that leaven, that bitter spirit, out of us.

precepts.text: To be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. The carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God. When you are spiritually minded you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean always being buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers want to hold on to that rival feeling, waiting to get back at the brother; that is the carnal mind.
precepts.point: For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Esau was a man of the field and a profane person: his religion is sin. Paul gives the name for that mind: “For to be carnally minded is death.” To be carnally minded is to be Edomite minded, the profane mind. It is death, and that is why he is called the son of perdition.

“but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” When you are spiritually minded, you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean we always have to be buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers turn a brother into an enemy like a rival team in sports, stay pumped up against him and hold on to that feeling, waiting to get back at him. That is the carnal mind. Stay in the spirit.

“Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God.” The Edomite mind, the mind of the spirit of Cain, goes against God and is not subject to his law.

So there are the children of God and the children of the devil, with no in between: either the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The bitter spirit that holds a grudge against a brother is the carnal mind of Esau, and it leads to the same death and rejection he found.

precepts.text: But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes? You are talking about in God we trust, swearing in on the Bible, and doing nothing according to the scriptures. Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee: the carnal mind is at war with God. This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too.
precepts.point: For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
This is the Edomite mindset, the carnal mind at war with God. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Unto the wicked, the white man, God says: hold on, you are carnally minded. Why are you out there talking about in God we trust? Why are you swearing in on the Bible when you do nothing according to the scriptures?

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” He talks about in God we trust while he has transgenders out there, putting two men together. They don't do anything the scriptures say. They cast the word behind their back, because the carnal mind is at war with God.

This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. It is the same profane spirit Hebrews names in Esau, whose religion is sin and who despised what was sacred. So we have to make sure we stand in the spirit, and not take God's covenant in our mouth while we cast his words behind us, as a brother does when he holds on to a bitter spirit.

precepts.text: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. The one that spake on earth was Moses; the people said, we do not want God to speak to us, Moses, you tell us the commandments, because his voice shook the earth and they were terrified. Much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven: that was the Lord. Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven: that is when he returns in the future to shake the nations. For our God is a consuming fire: that is what the people saw when he came down on the mountain.
precepts.point: Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice: whose voice did they hear from the heavens? That was Christ's voice, speaking the commandments. And upon earth he shewed thee his great fire: when the Lord came down in Exodus, only the seventy elders saw his majesty; everybody else saw fire.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Paul speaks of the same thing Moses did in Deuteronomy 4. “See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth”: the one that spoke on earth is Moses. The people said, we do not want to hear God, lest we die; Moses, you tell us what he says. Moses gave us the laws, we refused them from Moses, and everybody was killed in the wilderness.

“much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven”. The one speaking from heaven was the Lord. “Whose voice then shook the earth”. When he spoke the commandments the earth was shaking, and that is why the people were terrified and said, Moses, you speak to us. “but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.” He is going to shake nations: that is when he returns in the future. The Lord already knew we would go off and that he would have to come again to deliver us. Then those things “which cannot be shaken may remain”, and we receive “a kingdom which cannot be moved”.

“For our God is a consuming fire.” Why does Paul say this? Because that is what the people saw. The Lord said, do not let anybody come near the mountain when I come down, because anyone who comes near will die. When he came down it was a consuming fire; that is all everybody saw, except the seventy elders, who had the Holy Spirit on them and saw his majesty. That is Deuteronomy 4:36: “upon earth he shewed thee his great fire; and thou heardest his words out of the midst of the fire”, the fire that issues forth from his throne.

precepts.text: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck: corrected until correction is void, then bitter, then out the door with wife and children.
precepts.point: For one morsel of meat he sold his birthright: your trinkets are a morsel of meat, and afterward Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance though he sought it with tears. That will be many bitter brothers and sisters in that day, and Christ will say I never knew thee.
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Where does that root come from? Proverbs answers: “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck”. He that is often corrected hardens his neck, meaning his mind. You can't tell that brother nothing: I'm a man, you a man, I do what I want. Well, do what you want and burn by yourself.

That is the mindset of a lot of our brothers and sisters. They never took the scripture serious. Leadership corrects them, corrects them, corrects them, to the point where the correction is null and void, because they are not going to apply anything. After a while the Lord says, this spirit is rebellious as hell; he always hardens his mind and doesn't give a damn what you're saying.

You end up hardening your heart from always having correction done to you, until at the end of the day bitterness is formed, and then you're out the door with your wife and your children.

So the question for every brother and sister: are you one of the many that shall be offended when correction comes, when the men are told to get their homes in order and the women to be that pillar of rest and not stress? Or will you get in check with the Lord? The bitterness of Hebrews 12 grows out of a neck hardened against reproof.

precepts.text: Set thou a wicked man over him and let Satan stand at his right hand; let his prayer become sin, his days be few and another take his office: the lot of those who revile the hoary head and rise against leadership, as in 2018.
precepts.point: For one morsel of meat he sold his birthright: your trinkets are a morsel of meat, and afterward Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance though he sought it with tears. That will be many bitter brothers and sisters in that day, and Christ will say I never knew thee.
precepts.why:
Hebrews says “Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau”. Paul is comparing the wicked of our people to Esau, who was wicked and estranged from the womb and went to the Canaanitish women when he wanted to get married. The bitter among us become compared to Edom, and Satan becomes their daddy. Psalms shows it: “Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That wicked man is Satan, the daddy of Esau and of the wicked of our people.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Why does his prayer become sin? Because Christ said if you have an ought with your brother, go to him; leave your gift at the altar. You can't come to the Lord while the matter between you and your brother and your sister is not dealt with right. In 2018 there were extortioners speaking against leadership. You are not supposed to rise up against the hoary head; you are supposed to honor, and not revile the gods, your leaders. There was a lot of disrespect and dishonor.

“Let his days be few; and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.” That is what happens when Satan becomes your daddy. Repent.

So the profane spirit of Hebrews 12, the bitter brother or sister who turns on leadership, carries this lot. We are trying to encourage our people not to be worldly, not to keep the customs of Edom and the I-do-me, but to come back home to your people.

precepts.text: Lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily besets us and run the race with patience: you cannot win a race on a timer while carrying weights, and walking it is not winning at all.
precepts.point: Left undressed, like a lawn never mowed, the field is cast into the fire. Reject help and stay to yourself and destruction is the only thing left.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
The Lord says to them who keep his commandments and precepts, “let not your sins weigh you down.” Sin feels good. The pleasure comes, and once the pleasure is gone the guilt rolls in, and you feel like crap. After a while it becomes a burden, and it shows on you. Many of us came into the school guilty of things too shameful to confess, and some are still doing them. When you come forward and confess, you feel that weight lifted off: thank God.

Paul uses the same picture: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.” Lay aside every weight. Your sins of character are weights.

If you run a race carrying weights, can you run fast? No. You can still be in the race, but you either keep adding weight until you come in last and never cross the finish line, or you take the weights off. One weight off and you feel lighter; another off and you are faster. You were in third, now second, now first.

Some of y’all say, I’m good back here, I’ll just walk. Meanwhile you are on a timer, and time at the end is running out. A race is won by the time you run. If you are walking in a race, you are not winning at all, by no account.

That is why we lay aside every weight: the sins that so easily beset us are what hold us back. It is what 2 Esdras means: do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.text: Lay aside every weight and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and run with patience the race. Wisdom of Solomon 9:15: the corruptible body presseth down the soul. Some things stop when you come in, pork, Sabbath-breaking, the beard, but lust, hatred, and covetousness do not go away; you learn to keep that Negro or Latino in check until you die or Christ returns. Do not worry about the war in Iran; God has that. Worry about the day-to-day war.
precepts.point: We look not at the things which are seen, which are temporal, but at the things not seen, which are eternal. America influences the whole world in music and culture, but this power will fall; the kingdom we cannot see yet lasts forever. Stack your bricks and do not be a situational Israelite.
precepts.why:
“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight”: everything that is trying to keep us from serving our God. That is exactly what sin does. “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The earthly tabernacle is our flesh. We were born and shapen in iniquity, so understand the condition of the battle: we will fight against our flesh until we die or until Christ returns.

A lot of people think that when they come into the truth, things will just go away. Some things you stop doing: eating pork, breaking the Lord's Sabbath, not wearing fringes, shaving your beard. You start keeping the commandments, your reasonable service. But hatred, lust and covetousness do not go away. You learn how to cope with them, and you have to prove yourself to the Lord that you are able to keep that Negro in check, that Latino in check.

“and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us”. We do not have a lot of time left. Now is high time to wake up out of sleep and fight this battle right here. We are not worried about the war in Iran; God already has that. We need to worry about the war on the day-to-day.

That is looking at the things which are not seen: running the race with patience toward the eternal, not weighed down by the temporal.

precepts.text: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you. Not occupied in the work and the study, bitterness springs up; separate from your people and Satan plays on your psyche: they never liked you anyway. 1 Peter 5:8, be sober and vigilant, for the devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, as he desired to sift Peter.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.
precepts.why:
“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.” We have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we are not, we can fall from the grace of God.

“lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” If you are not occupied in doing the Lord’s work, not putting your hands to the plow, not studying, not being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you are not studying to combat it. You might have a feeling, but you had better rebuke that thing, and the way to do it is to be around these people.

If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your psyche and your mind. When you are not constantly seeing people you start thinking differently: they never liked you anyway. That is what Satan does.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan wants to devour all of us, just as Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him to sift him as wheat. We have to be in that mindset and know what is going on. The hasty man who does not look diligently lets bitterness spring up, and he is worse off than a fool.

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.
precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” Whom the Lord loves, he chastises. This is why we go through things in our lives that we might not like at the moment. It is the same thing Job 5:17 says: “happy is the man whom God correcteth.”

“And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” So if you are in this truth, expect to get scourged. Expect to get beat.

“If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” If you endure that chastisement, God is dealing with you like a son. “But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” Nobody wants to be a bastard. So “despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty”: the chastening is the proof that you are his son.

precepts.text: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence. And we what? And we gave them reverence. What is another term for reverence? Respect. Honour. Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits? So now even more so we have got to respect the Lord that created us, even more so. But we still have to have respect and honour and reverence for our earthly fathers. Thus saith the Lord.
precepts.point: You make an atonement for your sins when you do that. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Let us see why.
precepts.why:
“Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, and that goes for your mother too. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Hebrews shows why.

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence”. Another word for reverence is respect, honour. The fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them that honour.

“Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” So even more so we have to respect the Lord that created us. But that does not cancel the first part: we still have to have respect, honour and reverence for our earthly fathers. Thus saith the Lord. Honouring the father of your flesh is part of being in subjection to the Father of spirits, and that is why it makes an atonement.

precepts.text: Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright, was rejected and found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
precepts.point: Esau found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He that despised the birthright for one morsel of meat was rejected when he would have inherited the blessing.
precepts.why:
Esau “cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry”, and “lifted up his voice, and wept”: “Bless me, even me also, O my father.” But he had already sold the birthright and never dealt rightly with Jacob about it; he wanted the blessing anyway.

Paul names him: “any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.”

He that despised the birthright for one morsel of meat was rejected when he would have inherited the blessing. The tears in Genesis 27 are the tears in Hebrews 12, and they found no place of repentance.

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth; if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
precepts.point: This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?”

Moses says the same: “as a man chasteneth his son, so the Lord thy God chasteneth thee.” You do wrong, you get punished, exactly as a father raises his children. Who is more experienced than the Most High, the Ancient of days? There is no way we can tell him through our actions that we know what is right for us.

“But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people.

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.”

Moses says the same: “as a man chasteneth his son, so the Lord thy God chasteneth thee.” It is not joyous when you do wrong and get punished, but that is exactly how a father raises his children, and afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness. Who is more experienced than the Most High, the Ancient of days? There is no way we can tell him through our actions that we know what is right for us. The other nations are not chastened because they are not the sons; Israel is, and we cannot do what they do.

A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us?

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon asks, “if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us?” A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us? Here is the answer. “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.”

“If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.”

That is why the other nations never suffer the judgments we suffer. The chastening of the Most High does not pertain to them; he chastens us because we are his sons. All this befell Israel in Gideon's day, and befalls us now, not because the Lord has forsaken us, but because he receives us as sons.

precepts.text: No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous but grievous, and it does look grievous to all of us; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness, which is the kingdom, eternal life, and everlasting peace for them which are exercised thereby.

A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us?

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” Our fathers “for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.”

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous.” It does look grievous to all of us, just as it looked to Gideon with Midian eating up the land. But “nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” That peaceable fruit is the kingdom, eternal life, and everlasting peace for them which are exercised by the chastening. So “why then is all this befallen us” has an answer: for our profit.

precepts.text: We gave the fathers of our flesh reverence; how much rather should we be in subjection to the Father of spirits, for the Most High deals with the spirits of men, not the outside.
precepts.point: This still happens today: brothers will look at a group and assume the biggest one must be the leader, not knowing that brother might be the soldier while the leader is the slim one beside him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” The Most High is the Father of spirits. He deals with the spirits of men, not the outside.

That is why Eliab’s countenance and the height of his stature meant nothing: “the Lord looketh on the heart.”

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth; they that are without the chastisement that all are partakers of are bastards and not sons, and Israel alone knows this chastisement.
precepts.point: Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary and given Jacob to the curse and Israel to reproaches. The Most High gave Jacob to the curse.
precepts.why:
The Most High gave Jacob to the curse, and that curse is chastisement: “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.”

Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth. They that are without the chastisement that all are partakers of are bastards and not sons, and Israel alone knows this chastisement. So Jacob given to the curse and Israel to reproaches is the Father dealing with sons: he is the same one “that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins”, who says, “Put me in remembrance: let us plead together”.

precepts.text: Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance though he sought it with tears, so salvation opening to Cornelius proves he was not of Esau's Rome.
precepts.point: Scholars also record that Esau is the forefather of the Roman Empire, so if Cornelius were truly a Roman he would be an Edomite, and the Most High rejected Esau. This is the proof that Cornelius could not be a Roman by nation, because a Roman would have no place of repentance.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.”

Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance, though he sought it with tears. A Roman, being of Esau, would have no place of repentance. So salvation opening to Cornelius is the proof that he was not of Esau's Rome. He could not be a Roman by nation.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. A lot of times we hate to be chastened; we do. Paul says the same thing here. “And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children,” because we are children, “My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord,” Christ said, as many as I love I chasten, I rebuke. “nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:” You know what it means by don't faint? Don't give up, don't run, don't go, I'm leaving, I'm going back, I'm going to put a head wrap on my head and sing. You idiot.

“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” He scourges every son that he receives. So that is what has happened to all of us, and it is going to intensify; he is trying us. “If ye endure chastening,” Deacon Malachi said today he sees in the spirit that things could possibly get worse here in Babylon the great for us, but the Lord is going to look out for us. If you endure whatever comes our way, brothers and sisters, we must endure. “God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” What son is he that the father does not chasten, does not punish?

“But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers,” You see that: which all are partakers of. You are not going to come into this truth and not be chastened of the Lord. You are not going to be called into this truth and not be chastened of the Lord; only if you're an agent, and he wasn't called, he was sent. “then are ye bastards,” Then are ye bastards. Did you hear that, Weasel? Then are ye bastards, “and not sons.” You are not sons of God.

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence:” If your own earthly father corrects you, and I ain't talking about those of you with crackhead fathers or fathers on methadone, we gave them reverence. “shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” The Father of spirits, that is the Lord. “For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure;” Your own earthly father would chasten you for a few days after his own pleasure: you didn't wash the dishes, I'm going to beat you on the sides and you don't get no TV for a week. “but he for our profit,” God chastens us for our profit, meaning there is a divine reason, a spiritual reason, for God to chasten us. “that we might be partakers of his holiness.” He wants us to be partakers of his holiness, but in order to become partakers we must be chastened. He has to beat certain characteristics out of us, train us.

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous,” Like this thing going on now; it doesn't seem joyous at all. “but grievous:” Some of you lost your jobs; this is grievous. Lord Jesus, help me, I don't know what I'm going to do. Just hang on in there, just hold on. If it's food, we got you. If everybody loses their job there is nothing we could really do, we go bankrupt, we'd be in the damn street, but food and clothes, we got you. The government said they are going to give out stimulus packages, and we are going to roll with that. And for you Negroes that talk about how 501c3 is so evil, so wicked, because you are getting government handouts: then don't take the government stimulus package, you black-ass devils. Don't take the check at all. That is a covenant with the government. You are going to take that, but we're evil? Yeah, right. “nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” What does that mean? Once you come through that fire you can look back at the chastening and say, God was trying to teach me something; now I understand what he was trying to show me. I didn't understand it at the moment, but I see it now. Hindsight is 20/20.

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;” Right now we are going through this thing in the country: hands are hanging down, knees are quaking, we don't know what the Lord is going to do. Lift up the hands which hang down, meaning lift up your hands to pray; and your feeble knees, strengthen them knees. “And make straight paths for your feet,” Meaning walk straight in the laws of God, in the plans of God. “lest that which is lame be turned out of the way;” See them brothers and sisters that left this truth: they were lame, all lame, and were turned out of the way. Why? Because when they got some chastisement they said, I'm leaving, I'm gone, you're the devil, I hate you. Now you are lame and turned out of the way, because you couldn't endure the chastening of the Lord. “but let it rather be healed.”

points: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled. The root of bitterness starts very small. And it says many are defiled by that root of bitterness. It is not what I say, it is what God says. God says many are defiled by that root of bitterness.
Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.
For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.

Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. Following peace is the same thing as endeavouring to keep the unity. It takes effort. You cannot follow peace and at the same time be harbouring and nourishing hatred. The two do not work at the same time. And holiness: keeping the commandments of God, not letting the sun go down on your wrath. Because if you do not do that, what is the end result? No man shall see the Lord. That is why this is so important, because you cannot hate your brother whom you can see and then say you love God whom you cannot see. God said, you do not have to worry about seeing me, because you are not going to see me, because I died for the person that you are harbouring hatred against. I forgave the person that you hate many Days of Atonement ago. But you are still holding on to the thing that they fasted for.

Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled. A root of bitterness. Bitterness develops hatred. Hatred is actually murder. When you hold bitterness, some of you hold it for so long, and that goes back to trauma, that it starts affecting your health. It affects the way you think. It affects the way you look at things. Your wife might do something to you, or a brother might do something to you, and you hold that bitterness for so long that you do not look at the person the same any more. You are waiting for something to happen so you can use that spirit to get out of the situation. You use that bitterness as an excuse to do evil to each other.

Skewing your view of others. You start looking at others differently, and that person you look at differently did nothing to you. Let us say you have bitterness towards a brother. Now your wife starts looking at his wife differently. Whatever you and that brother have going on has nothing to do with your wives. But because of that bitterness you tell your wife what you think about that brother, and now she starts looking at that sister differently, when your wife and that sister were good until now. Because of that evil seed you put in her. So now, because of bitterness, you put division on that side too.

Bitterness is a hidden root that eventually produces visible damage. Signs of bitterness: repeatedly revisiting the offence. Speaking negatively about the offender. Difficulty praying for each other or for others. Refusing reconciliation. Generalised mistrust of others.

Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. In that pottage was meat: feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage, raw, bloody meat. And you have brothers today lusting after these same people. Many times brothers ask what it means that Esau was profane or a fornicator; the scriptures explain it.
For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: rejected by God; for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.

Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us: everybody has that one sin that is hard to fight. And let us run with patience the race that is set before us: you cannot run this race fast.

Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross. He could have called angels, but he had to endure it, despising the shame. Consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds. Some people become weary and give up and go back into the world, because nobody wants to suffer; and it starts in your mind. We have to use how Christ suffered as our example.

Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin. Right now we are all being built up, but we have not resisted unto blood yet. What does that mean? When Christ said, whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny, it is talking about when your life is on the line: whether you will turn your back on Christ while you are being persecuted, being tortured, facing years in prison for teaching the word of God. That is resisting unto blood: enduring this truth while you go through that. Some of you will remember this class and say, Deacon talked about these things, because I see what is coming.

My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: for whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. Why are bad things happening to you? Because God loves you.

If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons. If you are not going through anything, either you belong to Satan, or the Lord is just not ready for you yet; he is still building you up. All of us have to go through things; that is what molds us and makes us perfect.

Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby. When you go through things, that affliction and correction make you better; you bring forth fruits.

Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees: because sometimes when things go bad in your life, or you get corrected, you hang your hands down, sad all the time. Make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way: you do not want to be in this truth four or five years and turn back into the world because of correction. But let it rather be healed. Let that correction heal you; do not sit and listen to Satan telling you they hate you.

Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. You could end up hating the person that corrected you; if you become bitter over correction, you are not going to see God.

Looking diligently lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled. If you sit and listen to Satan, he puts evil thoughts in your mind, and now you are carrying hatred and trouble in your mind.

Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. That goes into bitterness, and it goes into this: when a brother comes and gives up his rank, that is no different from Esau giving up his birthright. We put you over men, you have a position, and you say, I do not want this responsibility? If you need help, ask for help, and we will send a brother to help you. But giving it up is like spitting in Christ's face; and when you give up your rank, you are not getting it back.

For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth. Why would he correct us or rebuke us if he did not love us? The correction comes because of the love, not the opposite. If he did not love us, he would cut us off; look at Esau: he cut him off because he hates him.

For what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? As a father you have to correct your son, because if you do not correct him, you do not love him; and as a father you want to see your son do better than you. It is the same in the truth: the heads of the school are fathers over the congregation and treat you as sons, and our leadership are fathers over us; we get chastised just as much as you do, if not more. But that is out of love. And some will turn their back to that and take their ball and go home.

Looking diligently: it is not talking about looking over the horizon; you have to look within yourself. Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you: that is the subterranean sin that no one can see. Over time it springs up and troubles you: it distorts your thoughts and alters your perception of reality. To the pure all things are pure; when that root comes in, the things that were once pure are no longer pure. And thereby many be defiled.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: When he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: and if you roll in the spirit of bitterness, you are a spiritual Edomite. Brothers talk about being a spiritual Israelite; with the bitter spirit you are the opposite on the inside, and always the victim.

For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: How can a man fail of the grace of God? When God says something and you refuse to do it. Esau despised his birthright; that is when you fall from the grace of God.
Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you: Esau became bitter after that, and thereby many were defiled.

Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. When he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He wept before his father, but the deed was already done and the Lord's will was done.

Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau: there are fornicators and profane people, but nobody reached the level of Esau when it comes to fornication and profaneness. He topped everybody.
Who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright: and when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected.
For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: none. That means he cannot be saved. Though he cried, he is not getting it.

Look diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God: it is your job to assess yourself, keep up with current events and read your four chapters a day, because the Lord has already given the mysteries and it is for us to apply them.

You fall from grace when the world and your job become your god; then correction from a brother or sister offends you, and a root of bitterness springs up, as happened with a captain's own number two who now hates him.
That root of bitterness is the catalyst for many to be defiled: they go back into the doctrines, holidays and philosophies of the society they were comfortable in.

Lest there be any fornicator or profane person as Esau: profane is devoted to what is not sacred, worldly, concerned with material values rather than a spiritual existence. The bitter among our people are likened to Esau, and Satan becomes their daddy.

For one morsel of meat he sold his birthright: your trinkets are a morsel of meat, and afterward Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance though he sought it with tears. That will be many bitter brothers and sisters in that day, and Christ will say I never knew thee.
